name: application-empty-search-suggestions
title: Empty Search Suggestions
description: No-results search state offering clickable popular or related query suggestions to help the user recover — distinct from application-no-results-search-state, which offers only a clear-filters action with no query suggestions.
useWhen: A search returns zero results and you have popular or related search terms to suggest instead.
A likely spelling correction is available for the user's query (a 'Did you mean' suggestion).
Offering category browsing as a recovery path when the specific search term didn't match anything.
avoidWhen: No real suggestions or corrections are available — use application-no-results-search-state's simpler clear-filters message instead of fabricating suggestions.
The empty state isn't from a search at all (e.g. a genuinely empty list) — use application-empty-states instead.
Filters, not the search term, caused zero results — a clear-filters action is more useful than search suggestions.
responsiveBehavior: The card has a fixed max width; suggestion chips wrap onto multiple lines as needed at narrow widths.
accessibility: The searched query is echoed back in real text so users can confirm what didn't match.
Suggestion chips and the 'Did you mean' correction are real buttons, not styled spans, so they are keyboard-operable.
The category label uses a real heading-like text element to group the suggestion chips for screen reader users.

variants.title: Popular searches
variants.description: No-results state with a row of clickable popular-search chips.
accessibility: Each suggestion chip is a real button with its own accessible name (the suggested term).

variants.title: Popular searches (Dark)
variants.description: Popular-searches empty state adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Chip border and text contrast must meet WCAG AA on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: Did you mean + categories
variants.description: No-results state with a spelling-correction suggestion and a row of category chips to browse instead.
accessibility: The 'Did you mean' correction is a real button, not a link styled to look clickable without being one.

variants.title: Did you mean + categories (Dark)
variants.description: Spelling-correction and category-chip empty state adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Category chip and correction-link contrast must meet WCAG AA on dark backgrounds.
